newsitem.title: USA: Continental Q2 passenger rev,load factor up.
newsitem.headline: Continental Q2 passenger rev,load factor up.

text.p: Continental Airlines said Wednesday its passenger revenue, load factor and cost per available miles all rose in the second quarter.
Passenger revenue rose 8.4 percent to $1.6 billion. The company said all routes added in the last year are performing better than forecast.
Continental's load factor grew to 72.3 percent compared to 69.5 percent in the same quarter of 1996.

Second quarter cost per available seat mile was $0.089 cents, up one percent as the company offset increases in fuel prices and wages and salaries with productivity savings and reductions in aircraft ownership costs.

The company said its pre-tax quarterly income of $208 million is "especially significant" because the aviation ticket tax was imposed during the second quarter of 1997, but not during the second quarter of 1996.
It also said it faced a weakened yen and higher fuel prices during the second quarter of 1997 compared to the same period in 1996.
After income taxes, the company reported diluted earnings per share of $1.64 compared to $2.04, and primary earnings per share of $2.01 compared to $2.53.
